2.cnNote: Good things come in pairs, so 2 is welcome.

3.cnNote: Sounds like 生 (life), but can also suggest 散 (split up).

4.angel: stability, hard work and solid foundations
4.jpNote: Shi sounds like death, so many say yon instead.
4.krNote: Sa sounds like death; lifts often label the 4th floor F.

5.cnNote: Linked to the Five Elements; neutral.

6.cnNote: Linked to smoothness, as in the saying 六六大顺 (everything goes smoothly).

7.cnNote: Neutral; the seventh lunar month holds the Ghost Festival.
7.jpNote: Lucky: Japan honours the Seven Lucky Gods.

8.cnNote: Sounds like 发 (prosper); the luckiest digit.
8.jpNote: Lucky: the character 八 widens at the base, a sign of growing fortune.

9.jpNote: Ku sounds like 苦 (suffering), so kyū is preferred.
9.thNote: Kao sounds like ก้าว, to step forward.

7.note: Widely seen as lucky in the West, and Japan honours Seven Lucky Gods.

777.note: Triple seven, the slot-machine jackpot, is a Western symbol of luck.

13.note: Feared in Western superstition (triskaidekaphobia), yet often lucky in Italy.

17.note: Unlucky in Italy: XVII rearranges to VIXI, Latin for 'I have lived'.

18.note: In Judaism, 18 spells chai ('life'); gifts often come in multiples of 18.

39.note: Avoided in Afghanistan (the 'curse of 39'); read san-kyū, 'thank you', in Japan.

44.note: Double 4 doubles the 'death' sound in Chinese, Japanese and Korean.

14.note: In Mandarin 1-4 can sound like 要死 ('want to die'), so it is often avoided.

88.note: Double 8 means double prosperity in Chinese; 88 is also chat slang for 'bye-bye'.

168.note: Read as 一路发, 'prosper all the way', in Chinese.

518.note: Read as 我要发, 'I will prosper', in Chinese.

520.note: Chinese internet slang for 'I love you'; 20 May is an unofficial Valentine's Day.

1314.note: 一生一世, 'a whole lifetime': popular in Chinese gift amounts and wedding dates.

250.note: 二百五 is Chinese slang for a fool, so it is avoided in gifts and prices.

666.note: The 'number of the beast' in the West, but 'smooth, awesome' in Chinese slang.

108.note: Sacred in Hinduism and Buddhism: prayer malas carry 108 beads.

786.note: Written by many South Asian Muslims as the abjad value of the Bismillah.

101.note: A classic Indian shagun (gift) amount: one more than a round sum signals a fresh start.

1.title: The Leader
1.text: Ones prefer to set their own course and start things others only talk about. The shadow side is impatience and a reluctance to ask for help.

2.title: The Diplomat
2.text: Twos read a room well and make partnerships work. The shadow side is self-doubt and avoiding necessary conflict.

3.title: The Communicator
3.text: Threes turn ideas into words, art and energy that lifts others. The shadow side is scattered focus.

4.title: The Builder
4.text: Fours build systems that last and keep promises. The shadow side is rigidity when plans change.

5.title: The Explorer
5.text: Fives thrive on movement, travel, trade and communication. The shadow side is restlessness and overcommitment.

6.title: The Nurturer
6.text: Sixes hold families, teams and communities together. The shadow side is carrying everyone else's load.

7.title: The Seeker
7.text: Sevens look beneath the surface and trust evidence they have checked themselves. The shadow side is isolation.

8.title: The Achiever
8.text: Eights manage money, power and scale with confidence. The shadow side is measuring worth only by results.

9.title: The Humanitarian
9.text: Nines see the bigger picture and finish what others abandon. The shadow side is difficulty letting go.

11.title: The Intuitive (master number)
11.text: Eleven is read as an amplified 2: strong intuition that inspires others, with nervous energy to manage.

22.title: The Master Builder (master number)
22.text: Twenty-two is read as an amplified 4: large ideas turned into real structures, if the pressure does not overwhelm.

33.title: The Master Teacher (master number)
33.text: Thirty-three is read as an amplified 6: care expressed by teaching and uplifting many people.

sq.label: Perfect square
sq.desc: A whole number multiplied by itself.

cu.label: Perfect cube
cu.desc: A whole number raised to the third power.

tr.label: Triangular
tr.desc: Dots that form a triangle: 1, 3, 6, 10 and so on.

pa.label: Palindrome
pa.desc: Reads the same forwards and backwards.

ha.label: Harshad
ha.desc: Divisible by the sum of its digits.

ar.label: Armstrong
ar.desc: Equals the sum of its digits, each raised to the number of digits.

hp.label: Happy
hp.desc: Repeatedly summing the squares of its digits reaches 1.

pf.label: Perfect
pf.desc: Equals the sum of its proper divisors.

ab.label: Abundant
ab.desc: Its proper divisors add up to more than the number.

de.label: Deficient
de.desc: Its proper divisors add up to less than the number.

se.label: Semiprime
se.desc: The product of exactly two primes.

p2.label: Power of two
p2.desc: 2 multiplied by itself some number of times.

tw.label: Twin prime
tw.desc: A prime that sits 2 away from another prime.

sg.label: Sophie Germain prime
sg.desc: A prime p where 2p + 1 is also prime.

sa.label: Safe prime
sa.desc: A prime p where (p − 1) ÷ 2 is also prime.

em.label: Emirp
em.desc: A prime whose reversed digits form a different prime.

aa.label: ABCABC number
aa.desc: A 3-digit block written twice, so always divisible by 7, 11 and 13.
